板.meaning: A lumberjack swings at a grumpy <part>tree</part>, but it's <part>anti</part> everything: anti-axe, anti-saw, anti-chainsaw. In the end it agrees to give up one flat slice of itself, if he promises to make it into a pirate's walkway. He gets a single <kanji>plank</kanji>.
板.on: Pirates later stroll along it, munching sticky <sound>bun</sound> after sticky bun.
板.kun: One pirate wobbles on the end, squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>!' and drops his <sound>ta</sound>co into the sea.

訪.meaning: Your grandma arrives by boat, unfurls her <part>sail</part> in your front garden and gives a long <part>speech</part> from the deck about how much you've grown. She stays for tea, three naps and two weeks. That's how she likes to <kanji>call on</kanji> you.
訪.on: You hint it's time to go by spraying her deck with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
訪.kun: Next year she's back, with an <sound>o</sound>ctopus on <sound>to</sound>p of the mast and a basket of yu<sound>zu</sound> fruit for you.

脳.meaning: A <part>villain</part> wears a bucket on his head to stop his ideas leaking out. It fails: one night <part>fireworks</part> burst out of the bucket and spell his whole evil plan across the <part>moon</part>. Now the entire town can read his <kanji>brain</kanji>.
脳.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me reads the plan in the sky and calls the police.
脳.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' he groans, hurling a yu<sound>zu</sound> at a <sound>roo</sound>k that is cawing his plan to the whole town.

聴.meaning: A shy whale sings at the bottom of the sea, so a fisherman lowers a <part>net</part> with <part>ten</part> seashells tied to it, presses one <part>ear</part> to the rope and holds his breath. The song trembles up the line and straight into his <part>heart</part>. For once he stops talking, to <kanji>listen</kanji>.
聴.on: The tune is so lovely that his collar feels as tight as a <sound>cho</sound>ker.
聴.kun: Back on shore, he hums it to a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird and the ship's <sound>coo</sound>k, who lean in close.

講.meaning: A professor refuses to use the stage, so she climbs the wobbly <part>scaffolding</part> outside the hall and gives her <part>speech</part> through a third-floor window, swaying with every point. Students below take notes with their necks craned. It's the scariest <kanji>lecture</kanji> on campus.
講.on: She points at her slides with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, dripping on the front row.

京.meaning: The king builds his city on a giant cooking pot: the palace sits on the <part>lid</part>, the market squeezes into the pot's <part>mouth</part>, and a <part>little</part> village dangles from the legs below. Every road leads up to the lid, where the king sits waving. It's the nation's <kanji>capital</kanji>.
京.on: From the lid, the king bangs a gong and calls out his city's name, <sound>Kyo</sound>to, holding its first part so long it echoes down the pot to the village.
京.kun: Down there, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat knits <sound>ya</sound>rn into a scarf for a shivering <sound>ko</sound>ala.

版.meaning: Before each print run, the old editor holds a <part>tai chi pose</part> on the roof. Today a rival paper prints the <part>anti</part> of every headline he wrote, so he flows slowly downstairs and prints a reply, then a reply to their reply. By sunset six versions are on sale, each a fresh <kanji>edition</kanji>.
版.on: The ink smells sweet, because the cheap print shop has mixed it with <sound>hon</sound>ey.

暮.meaning: The <part>sunset</part> is so lovely that a second <part>sun</part> sinks down to join it and refuses to leave, peeking over the hill. Owls wake up confused, bats don't know whether to go out, and the sky stays purple for hours. The whole town is stuck in <kanji>twilight</kanji>.
暮.on: An old man waters his <sound>bo</sound>nsai on the porch, glad of the long purple glow.
暮.kun: Finally a <sound>coo</sound>k gives up waiting and lights the lamps as the day grows dark.

第.meaning: Under a roof of <part>bamboo</part>, a pompous goose holds a <part>funeral</part> for its old toothbrush, and the mourners line up by height. A <part>slash</part> of chalk on each forehead marks who's first, second and third. Everybody knows their <kanji>ordinal</kanji> place.
第.on: Late arrivals roll the <sound>di</sound>ce to decide who gets to be fourth.

施.meaning: The captain's orders are clear: hoist the <part>sail</part>, polish the <part>diving board</part>, and teach the ship's <part>scorpion</part> to juggle. The crew grumbles but does every single one, the scorpion included. A good crew will <kanji>carry out</kanji> any order.
施.on: The scorpion juggles behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld, just in case its tail slips.
施.kun: Afterwards the captain gives a <sound>ho</sound>tdog to a <sound>do</sound>lphin and a <sound>ko</sound>ala who helped.

清.meaning: A fussy mermaid scrubs her lagoon every morning, flicking <part>water drops</part> off a brush until the whole bay shines a bright <part>blue</part>. Not one speck of sand, not one floating crumb. The water is so clean it's <kanji>pure</kanji>.
清.on: She keeps her brush locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe on the seabed.
清.kun: Even her lunch is spotless: a peeled <sound>ki</sound>wi and a pot of white <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

標.meaning: Voters keep getting lost on the way to the polls, so the mayor nails a giant <part>ballot</part> to a <part>tree</part> at the crossroads, with an arrow drawn on it. Birds sit on the arrow and spin it round, and now everyone ends up at the beach. At least it's a <kanji>signpost</kanji>.
標.on: At the beach, a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls does <sound>yo</sound>-yo tricks right under the sign.
標.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p and a <sound>roo</sound>k drag a <sound>be</sound>d up to the sign, planning to sleep right under it.

岸.meaning: A giant hangs her laundry on a <part>drying rack</part> balanced on a <part>cliff</part> beneath a <part>mountain</part>, and the wind blows her socks out to sea. Each one washes up on a different beach. Every morning she walks along the <kanji>shore</kanji> collecting them.
岸.on: One sock comes back full of green <sound>gun</sound>k from the rock pools.
岸.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird uses another sock as a <sound>shee</sound>t to nap on the sand.

訴.meaning: In the forest court, a squirrel gives a furious <part>speech</part>, pointing at a woodpecker: 'He drilled through my front door!' The woodpecker tries to <part>reject</part> it, but there's sawdust all over his beak. The owl judge hoots at the <kanji>accusation</kanji>.
訴.on: Then the judge sinks back on a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa to think it over.
訴.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps the crowd, as the squirrel p<sound>ut</sound>s a <sound>ta</sound>rt on the desk: 'Exhibit A, covered in sawdust!'

触.meaning: A deer is very proud of its <part>antler</part>, until one morning an <part>insect</part> lands on the tip and refuses to leave. The deer shakes, spins and sneezes, but every time the bug just taps it back with one leg. The two are in constant <kanji>contact</kanji>.
触.on: The deer rubs its antler on a woolly rug to scrape the bug off, then touches a metal gate and gets a crackling <sound>shock</sound> of static.
触.kun: The dazed deer lies down on a <sound>fu</sound>ton of moss, careful not to touch anything else.

課.meaning: At the jungle school, the gorilla teacher gives every <part>speech</part> with his mouth full of <part>fruit</part>, spraying mango over the front row. The monkeys write it all down on banana leaves and staple them into a book. Today they finish another juicy <kanji>chapter</kanji>.
課.on: The class pet, a fat <sound>ca</sound>rp in a bucket, gets all the mango peel.

府.meaning: A tiny town keeps adding things to its only garden <part>shed</part>: they <part>attach</part> a post office, then a library, then a bus stop, each nailed to the side. Soon the shed has its own mayor, flag and bin collection. It's become an official <kanji>borough</kanji>.
府.on: The mayor runs it all from a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the corner.

県.meaning: A nosy giant lies across the countryside with one <part>eye</part> open, keeping watch over the <part>little</part> farms between his fingers. Each farmer pays him a turnip a year to keep the foxes away. Everything he can see from there counts as one <kanji>prefecture</kanji>.
県.on: His pet wolf sleeps in a <sound>ken</sound>nel the size of a barn.
県.kun: At supper time he hangs a <sound>ca</sound>rp from a hook above the kennel door.

幕.meaning: A theatre can't afford velvet, so the cleaner sews every beach <part>towel</part> in the building into one huge sheet, printed with a palm-tree <part>sunset</part>. When the play ends, it drops with a damp thump and a whiff of sun cream. That's the theatre's new <kanji>curtain</kanji>.
幕.on: Backstage it drips <sound>muc</sound>k from the beach all over the actors' shoes.
幕.kun: On <sound>to</sound>p of the rail, a stagehand cooks a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue, and smoke drifts through the <sound>ree</sound>ds painted along its hem.

砲.meaning: A tidy giant decides to <part>pack up</part> his rock collection and post it to his cousin, so he stuffs every <part>stone</part> into a long iron tube and lights the end. Boom: the parcel flies over three hills. He's invented express mail, by <kanji>cannon</kanji>.
砲.on: The cousin puts out the smoking rocks with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.

就.meaning: In the busy <part>capital</part>, a man with a <part>broken crutch</part> limps into the king's office with a long letter. 'This is about the potholes,' he says, waving it. The king sighs and reads every page of a letter <kanji>concerning</kanji> his roads.
就.on: As proof, the man also hands over his worn-out <sound>shoe</sound>.
就.kun: The king sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' into the letter, then takes his seat at the desk to deal with it.

幼.meaning: A baby in a high chair grips a tiny <part>twist</part> of pretzel and, with every scrap of <part>muscle</part>, bends the whole chair in half. The nurses stare. If he can do that already, imagine him at five. He's still in his <kanji>infancy</kanji>.
幼.on: His favourite toy is a <sound>yo</sound>-yo that he swings like a wrecking ball.
幼.kun: At lunch he waves a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a scrap of <sound>na</sound>an, far too little to eat any of them.

敵.meaning: Every night a moth flutters toward the <part>hanging lantern</part> on the porch, and every night grandpa waves it away with a paper <part>fan</part>. Flap, flap, swat, miss. They've fought for forty summers, and each respects the other: a true <kanji>enemy</kanji>.
敵.on: One night the moth sends him a <sound>tex</sound>t message: 'See you tomorrow.'
敵.kun: Grandpa stocks up for the next fight: a <sound>ca</sound>rp bone, a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>ki</sound>wi skin to throw.

授.meaning: An old sea captain hands his rusty <part>anchor</part> to the youngest sailor, who must <part>accept</part> it with both hands, though it's heavy. Along with it come fifty years of knots, storms and sea songs. Some things you can only <kanji>impart</kanji> in person.
授.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of seagulls watches from the rail and nods.
授.kun: He also hands over a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines and a yu<sound>zu</sound> for the long trip.

頼.meaning: A shipwrecked sailor clings to a <part>bundle</part> of driftwood with a <part>rubber duck</part> tied on top as a lookout. The duck squeaks left, he paddles left; it squeaks right, he paddles right. It's never been wrong yet. That duck has his total <kanji>trust</kanji>.
頼.on: It even steers him round a sleeping <sound>rhi</sound>no floating on its back.
頼.kun: He begs the duck for a <sound>ta</sound>co, but it only ties a k<sound>no</sound>t in his beard.

導.meaning: Lost on a foggy <part>road</part>, a hiker meets a ghost who points the way with a <part>golf club</part>: left at the cow, right at the puddle, straight on past the old windmill. He never speaks, he only swings. Still, it's excellent <kanji>guidance</kanji>.
導.on: With each swing, a ball of bread <sound>dough</sound> lands on the right path.
導.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat follows the trail with a lump of <sound>chee</sound>se, and a <sound>bee</sound>tle rides on its back.

迫.meaning: A shy penguin stands at the top of a <part>ramp</part> on a <part>white</part> iceberg, too scared to slide. Her friends push, cheer and wave fish at her: 'Go! Go! Now!' At last she gives in to the <kanji>urge</kanji>.
迫.on: At the bottom she crashes face first into a <sound>huc</sound>kleberry pie.
迫.kun: A red <sound>se</sound>tter barks, and her <sound>ma</sound>ma waddles closer and closer to see.

束.meaning: A greedy <part>tree</part> grows a <part>mouth</part> in its trunk and gulps down every stick that blows past. By autumn it's so stuffed that its branches bulge in all directions, held round the middle by its own bark. It looks like one giant <kanji>bundle</kanji>.
束.on: Out of its mouth pokes one smelly <sound>sock</sound> it swallowed by mistake.
束.kun: A woodcutter ties it up and drags it home to fuel a <sound>ta</sound>co <sound>ba</sound>rbecue.

奇.meaning: A <part>large</part> man stands on the roof of the town hall, giving his <part>approval</part> to everything below: 'Yes' to the pigeons, 'yes' to the rain, 'yes' to a cow wearing a hat. Nobody knows who he is or how he got up there. It's all very <kanji>strange</kanji>.
奇.on: At sunset he unlocks a tiny door in the chimney with a brass <sound>key</sound> and vanishes.
奇.kun: Next morning, a <sound>coo</sound>k finds a <sound>shee</sound>p up there instead, nodding at everything.

却.meaning: The postman goes to <part>stamp</part> your letter, but the ink pad is <part>gone</part>: a squirrel ran off with it. So he presses his thumb into blueberry jam and stamps that on the envelope <kanji>instead</kanji>.
却.on: Down by the river, the squirrel paddles off in a tiny ka<sound>yak</sound>.
却.kun: On the bank, a <sound>ca</sound>rp waves at the postman, holding up an <sound>e</sound>gg instead of the ink pad.
